title: Commission Plan Effective-Date Boundary (variant)
scenario_text:
Cirrus Analytics operates on a fiscal year that runs October 1 through September 30. The FY26 commission plan, published to the field on August 15, replaces the FY25 plan and becomes effective for all deals with a customer-signed contract execution date on or after October 1, 2025. The FY26 plan pays 6% of ARR as base commission plus a 4% multi-year accelerator on any term over 24 months. The FY25 plan pays 8% of ARR as base commission plus a 2% accelerator on ARR that clears the rep's annual quota.

Account Executive Mia Torres closed a three-year, $480,000 TCV / $160,000 ARR deal with the enterprise buyer Helion Freight. The Salesforce opportunity shows: Close Date September 28, Stage 'Closed Won'. The signed order form in DocuSign is countersigned by the Helion CFO on October 3 at 09:15 AM Eastern. NetSuite booked the deal on October 3 the same day. Mia's FY25 annual quota was $1,200,000 and she was at $1,050,000 in booked ARR before this deal, so the deal would have brought her over quota under the FY25 plan. Her Deal Desk approval memo notes 'submitted for FY25 payout as pre-effective.' Payroll is preparing the October commission run and asks which plan governs this deal.
question: Which commission structure should Payroll apply to Mia Torres's $480,000 deal, and what is the resulting commission owed?
choices: Apply the FY25 plan (8% base + 2% accelerator over quota) — commission of $48,000.
Apply the FY26 plan (6% base + 4% multi-year accelerator) — commission of $48,000.
Apply the FY26 plan (6% base + 4% multi-year accelerator) — commission of $28,800.
Withhold payment and escalate to the Compensation Committee for a case-by-case ruling.
changed_fact: The customer's countersignature (contract execution) date moved from September 28 (before the FY26 plan effective date of October 1) to October 3 (after the FY26 plan effective date).
